title: Low living bar with a brick hearth core and a south ribbon

furniture.item: Chimney breast with raised hearth plinth

decision_log.decision: Organise the room as two parallel bars: a 1.15 m service strip along the north wall (log store, hearth core, coat press, entry vestibule) and a 5.50 x 3.05 m sitting bar along the glazed south wall.
decision_log.rationale: Gathers every service function in one lower, narrower strip offset from the principal space, and makes the sitting bar read longer and lower than the 5.50 x 4.20 m room.

decision_log.decision: Fireplace on the north wall (the internal wall the entry comes through) as a 2.00 x 0.85 m projecting brick mass on a raised plinth, centred at x 1.90 m, west of the room centreline.
decision_log.rationale: The hearth reads as an internal masonry core standing between vestibule and sitting bar, not a surround on the exterior window wall, and shares no centreline with door (x 4.80) or window band (x 2.84).

decision_log.decision: South ribbon: four 0.90 m casement leaves between 0.32 m brick piers on a 1.22 m module, sill course 0.80 m, head 2.05 m, stopping 0.38 m / 0.56 m short of the corners - 3.60 m of glass (65 %) in a 4.56 m band (83 %).
decision_log.rationale: A continuous band of tall narrow lights on the regular pier module with continuous sill and head band, never a single picture window, stopping one pier short of each corner.

decision_log.decision: West end wall expressed as a full-width group of three casements between piers (3.34 m of 4.20 m) with asymmetric corner piers, rather than a faked prow.
decision_log.rationale: In a plain rectangular room the end wall becomes a window group between piers; the unequal corner piers keep the whole asymmetric.

decision_log.decision: Entry: flush 0.90 m oak door at the east end of the north wall, no surround or step, opening into a 1.80 x 1.25 m vestibule under a 2.05 m soffit, closed west by the coat press and south by a slatted oak screen, with a 0.95 m exit along the east wall; door centre 2.22 m from the nearest seat.
decision_log.rationale: A compressed, low-ceilinged vestibule beside a solid mass and a screen from which the room opens; the door sits at the end of a long wall, not centred opposite the hearth.

decision_log.decision: Flat ceiling at 2.30 m with a continuous 0.45 m wide dropped soffit band at 2.05 m around the room and over the whole vestibule; the chimney breast stops under it with a stone cap.
decision_log.rationale: The ceiling edge is a deep horizontal band oversailing window and door heads the way an eave oversails a wall; the ceiling stays flat.

decision_log.decision: Three horizontal datums run uninterrupted: 0.45 m seat/plinth slab (log store, hearth plinth, window bench), 0.80 m cast-stone sill course wrapping the south and west walls, 2.05 m head band.
decision_log.rationale: Continuous sill course, head band at door-head height and plinth slabs keep the room reading long and low with no vertical element emphasised.

decision_log.decision: Every masonry edge capped in pale honed cast stone (sill course, plinth slab, breast cap, screen plinth, planter rim); brick exposed only as horizontal coursing with struck horizontal joints.
decision_log.rationale: Dark brick bands between plain light horizontal strips; no vertical joints drawn.

decision_log.decision: Chimney breast as a plain brick slab 1.60 x 1.48 m with a 0.90 x 0.55 m firebox (wider than high), a row of four small square recesses at 0.30 m centres, and a plain stone cap; no mantel.
decision_log.rationale: The breast is a plain capped slab pierced by small recesses, the fireplace a plain brick opening with a stepped-out plinth and no ornament.

decision_log.decision: Joinery and furniture built from stacked slabs and square posts: oversailing table top with a thinner rail beneath, square block feet, stepped cap finials on the chair posts, square oak pulls on a grid, horizontal slats; no curved mouldings.
decision_log.rationale: Profiles are stacked rectangular layers rather than carved or turned.

decision_log.decision: Seating for five: built-in 3-seat window bench under leaves W2-W3 plus two oak-and-leather armchairs facing each other across a low table, all south of the 0.90 m corridor along the core.
decision_log.rationale: The bench slab continues the 0.45 m datum along the long wall and keeps the whole group facing the hearth without crossing the circulation.

decision_log.decision: Palette: tawny brick and pale stone bands dominant with warm lime plaster; oiled oak, oxblood leather, copper and stippled wool as warm accents; every surface matt.
decision_log.rationale: Dark brick bands between light horizontal strips at a warm temperature; no mirrored panels and no high-gloss wall finish.

decision_log.decision: Floor: 180 mm European oak boards, hardwax-oiled matt, laid east-west.
decision_log.rationale: Board joints run with the long axis to stretch the room.

decision_log.decision: Planting built in: a copper-lined brick trough with a stone rim on the sill course under leaf W1; no freestanding pots.
decision_log.rationale: Planting sits in low troughs on sills, capped like every other masonry edge.

decision_log.decision: Circulation: a 0.90 m clear path from the door down the east side of the vestibule, west along the front of the core to the hearth, then south between armchair and table to the bench.
decision_log.rationale: The room flows past the masonry core on its south face; nothing stands in the door swing.

decision_log.decision: Lighting: a continuous concealed cove strip along the inner edge of the soffit band, a square recessed downlight in the vestibule, two low copper pendants over the table and a stacked-block oak lamp on the log-store slab.
decision_log.rationale: Light is carried as one horizontal band at the head datum, with low warm points in the sitting group.

decision_log.decision: Glazing detailed as a straight-line leaded lattice (vertical ladder bars, chevron heads, a band of shallow lozenges above the sill) in thin oak frames.
decision_log.rationale: Where glass is detailed it is a straight-line leaded pattern; elsewhere plain thin frames.

decision_log.decision: No framed solid infill panels in either window band.
decision_log.rationale: A 'sometimes' rule only; the brief asks for a window ribbon, so the bands are left as lights.

conflicts.constraint: Must 2 - ribbon WINDOWS on one long wall
conflicts.resolution: R11 wants floor-to-head glazed door leaves; the brief names windows, so the band is built as tall casements on a continuous 0.80 m sill course (R07). Brief favoured on element type; rule kept on module, short piers, outward swing and stopping one pier short of the corners.

conflicts.constraint: Room 5.50 x 4.20 m interior clear, ceiling 2.30 m (stated dimensions)
conflicts.resolution: The 1.31:1 plan cannot approach the corpus's long bar; dimensions kept exactly as briefed and the long-low reading made instead with the north service strip (sitting bar 5.50 x 3.05 m), the 0.45 m soffit band, three continuous datums and east-west boards.

conflicts.constraint: Must 1 - a fireplace/hearth element on one wall of a single room
conflicts.resolution: Hearth placed on the north wall, which reads internal because the entry arrives through it, as a projecting mass the room flows past on its south face and west flank. A true open passage past the flank into an adjoining room is not available in a one-room brief, so the 'passage past the core' is the 0.90 m corridor along its front.
